en: The Scripture on the Eight Yang Divine Mantras Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Mount Lingwu in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
The great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and one thousand bodhisattvas were present, all of whom were equal to Maitreya Bodhisattva and the others.
The Buddha addressed Śāriputra:

"To the east, passing from here beyond a world-system as numerous as the sands of one Ganges River, there is a buddha-field. There, a Buddha named Sukhāvatī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his land is called Invincible."

“Śāriputra! To the east, passing beyond two *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* [sands] of buddha-fields, there is a buddha-field where a Buddha named Candraketurāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently dwells and teaches the Dharma; his land is named Joyful Delight.”

“Śāriputra! To the east, passing beyond three *gaṅgā*-sands of buddha-fields, there is a buddha-field where the Buddha is named Samantaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma; his land is named Priyadarśana.”

“Śāriputra! To the east, passing beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in four Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field where the Buddha is named Vibhajya-atikrānta-viśuddha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He currently dwells there, teaching the Dharma; that land is named Naiguai.”

“Śāriputra! To the east, passing beyond five Ganges-sands of Buddha-fields, there is a Buddha-field where the Buddha is named Samaguṇaprabhāśiri Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He currently dwells there, teaching the Dharma; that land is named Vigatasaṃśaya.”

“Śāriputra! To the east, passing beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in six *gaṅgā* rivers, there is a buddha-field where the Buddha is named Mūlapādapaśirṣa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma; his land is named Avyāladaṃśa.”

“Śāriputra! To the east, passing beyond as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in seven Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field where a Buddha named Abhyatīta-ratnapadma Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, currently resides and teaches the Dharma; his land is named Padmagandhā.”

"Śāriputra! To the east, beyond worlds as numerous as the sands of eight Ganges Rivers, there is a buddha-field where a Buddha resides, named Ratnasaṃbhava-padma-sukhasthita-vṛkṣarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha. He is currently preaching the Dharma in a land called Madhuraghoṣābhiruta."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In the pure lands of the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, there are no five turbidities, no sensual desires, no women, no mental defilements, no curses, and no mutual disparagement."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If there are good men or good women who, upon hearing the names of these eight Buddhas, receive, uphold, recite, chant, read, and practice them, they shall never fall into the three evil realms, except for those who have committed the five grave offenses with no interval for repentance."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if these good sons and good daughters hold the names of these eight Buddhas and the names of their lands— those who receive, uphold, recite, and practice them— by virtue of this merit, if they give rise to the bodhicitta, in whatever place they are born, they will always encounter dhāraṇīs, always encounter the primary and secondary marks, always encounter the sounds of the marks, and always encounter the merit of circumambulation to the right."

If these good sons and good daughters practice and uphold these eight instructions of the Buddha, and act according to them correctly, they will be transformed from women into men wherever they are born.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if these good sons and good daughters, having washed and rinsed themselves clean at dawn and adjusted their robes, recite this sutra three times each during the day and night, they shall obtain immeasurable merit, and the first four heavenly kings will constantly protect them."
These sons and daughters of good family, whether they are among government officials,
or among enemies, or among bandits, or amidst water and fire,
or when encountering the terrors of wind and waves upon the great ocean, should read this sutra.
If one reads this sutra while amidst the fray of battle, or if one is afflicted by malevolent poisons, one should read this sutra;
if one hears the cries of evil birds or has a bad dream, one should read this sutra;
if one is struck by dragons or spirits, or if one is terrified with hair standing on end due to the influence of various māras, one should read this sutra.

Those who wish to do so should read this sutra; if there are those who face urgent fears, epidemics, or painful illnesses, they should recite this *Bhadrapāla-aṣṭamaṅgala-dhāraṇī-sūtra* over them, and they will immediately be cured.
At that time, the Buddha spoke these essential verses:
"In this land there is no Tathāgata; By upholding the name of this buddha-field, All evils shall be eliminated, And one will swiftly ascend the Path of Righteousness."
Wherever one is born, may one always encounter a Buddha; seeing the Awakened One brings great joy.
This Illuminator is the World-Honored One; serve him with an impartial mind.
For hundreds of eons, even beyond number, one should always remain free from attachment.
Swiftly attaining the path to Nirvāṇa, By revering the names of these Buddhas,
The present Tathāgatas now manifest, And uphold the names of their brilliant teachings.
Being simple, upright, and gentle, Wherever they are born, they shall behold them.
Possessing the marks of perfect symmetry and beauty, she was born into a family of many millions.
Valiant and fond of giving, she was not stingy or greedy toward others.
When the women heard this essential teaching, they leaped for joy with great delight.
Having cast off the female body, one shall be born as a man.
No soldiers dare to harm him; even those who practice sorcery bring no misfortune.
Neither government officials nor bandits will ever injure such a person.
"The five māras shall not be able to harass the generals, the officers, and their subordinates who uphold this sutra;
they shall find no opportunity to cause them harm.
At that time, the four Great Heavenly Kings and Maitreya Bodhisattva and others addressed the Buddha, saying:
"We shall together protect and uphold all students of this *Bhadra-pāla-vidyā-rāja-sūtra*; we shall exert our combined strength to protect them, so that those who are ill may be healed."
The Buddha said, "So it is.

The first Four Heavenly Kings, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and the assembly of bhikṣus, as well as the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and asuras, having heard this sutra, rejoiced and paid homage to the Buddha before departing.

The names of the eight bodhisattvas are: first, Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla; second, Bodhisattva Ratnākara; third, Bodhisattva Guhagupta; fourth, Bodhisattva Naradatta; fifth, Bodhisattva Susīma; sixth, Bodhisattva Indradatta; seventh, Bodhisattva Mahāsusārthavāha; and eighth, Bodhisattva Varuṇadeva. These eight have sought the Way for incalculable kalpas, yet they have not yet attained Buddhahood.
When these eight people were originally practicing the Way together, they made a vow that all the people of the eight directions and the zenith and nadir should together attain Buddhahood.
If anyone is in urgent distress, they should call upon the names of us eight; then their suffering shall be immediately relieved.
When their lifespan draws to a close, we eight shall fly through the air to welcome them.
May they hold fast to the merit of this single word; may all people enjoy the same joy as these eight bodhisattvas.
The Scripture on the Eight Yang Divine Incantations Spoken by the Buddha.
